text:
Maya: Heads up — CI microbench on PR #11050 tripped the perf gate (threshold diff). Looks like the new batch heuristic change reduced steady-state throughput and increased p95. Logging artifacts in the job.
Sam: Which metric regressed? can you paste the CI summary?
Maya: CI summary pasted by bot below, main deltas: throughput -6.8%, p95 +20ms, kv_hit_rate -9pp. Build: https://ci.internal/runs/11050
DeployBot: PR #11050 — microbench: THRESHOLD_DIFFFAIL (baseline vs branch)
  - batch_throughput: baseline=1200 req/s, branch=1118 req/s (-6.8%)
  - tail_latency_p95: baseline=48ms, branch=68ms (+20ms)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline=72%, branch=63% (-9pp)
Li: I ran a quick local repro on a dev rig. With the branch's batch timer tweak the scheduler waits longer for second-request coalescing which increases queueing; KV entries that would have been reused fall out of the small LRU window — hence hit_rate drop.
Anika: That matches telemetry from prod-ish smoke runs last week. We saw longer inter-arrival waits => batch size up sometimes but more variable, cache churn increased.
Kevin: Quick flamegraph from a short repro shows increased time in batch_assembler and kv_eviction. snippet:
```
batch_assembler  34% -> 47%
kv_cache::evict  4%  -> 14%
runtime_dispatch  18% -> 12%
```
Sam: Good catch. Can we bisect to the specific commit in the PR that introduced the heuristic change? Which file/commit?
Maya: The heuristic change is in pr diff: runtime/scheduler/batch_policy.cc commit 6b4f9e7 (touched wait_for_second_request logic). It was added in the feature branch as a single hunk.
Li: I ran a git bisect over the feature branch and narrowed it to that commit. Reverting that hunk locally brings throughput back to baseline and restores kv_hit_rate.
Anika: Given this is a CI gate fail on a heavy perf-critical path, can we mark PR as rollout-blocker and revert the change on main until we can tune? Need an owner to cut the revert.
Sam: I'll open a revert PR against the feature branch and main. Also will add the "perf-blocker" label and ping QA.
Maya: Revert PR opened: https://git.internal/pr/11070 — contains the revert of 6b4f9e7. Requesting quick CI cycle.
DeployBot: CI queued for revert PR 11070.
Kevin: For postmortem we should capture microbench config and a small synthetic load that reproduces the cache churn (inter-arrival ~20ms with occasional bursts). I'll attach a little harness.
Li: Repro command I used:
```
./perf_runner --workload=small-burst --i-arrival=20ms --duration=600 --batch-policy=branch
```
Maya: CI for revert passed (green). Metrics back to baseline. Please hold merges of other batching changes till we have a follow-up with improved guardrails (max-wait and cache-aware threshold).
Anika: Agreed. I'll create a ticket to add an automated perf test that simulates the inter-arrival distribution and flags kv_hit_rate regressions separately. Also suggest an integration test that runs the batch policy under an LRU-sized cache.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: @engineers oncall, watch for any rollout alerts this week; I'll coordinate the postmortem notes in the PR thread.
Kevin: I'll upload the profiler artifacts and add flamegraphs to the revert PR for the postmortem.
Maya: Thanks — closing this thread when docs/PR updated.
